# GameSurge — July 2002 promotional feature description

- Original source: [July 2002 news archive — Robin Hood item](https://gamesurge.com/archive/july2002.shtml)
- Author / publication: Falcon, posting credit; GameSurge.
- Language / date: English; 2002-07-24 (item posted 4:44 am PST under the "Wednesday, July 24, 2002" heading).
- Access: Full July 2002 archive page retrieved directly; the Robin Hood press-release item located within it
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: lookup failed (archive.org rate limit); not checked
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (press release as reposted by a commercial news site, not transcribed)

The promotional item describes more than forty missions divided into robbery/infiltration, castle attacks, and ambushes. It advertises selecting five characters, distinct abilities, and varied day, night, and fog presentations across towns and forest intersections. A winter 2002 retail window is given.

The text also markets environmental interactions such as climbing, entering buildings, operating traps, and lowering drawbridges. These are prerelease promotional claims rather than measured final-game coverage. Its sweeping claims of historical research and realism should be attributed to the publicity, not adopted as independent conclusions.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: the retrieved file is GameSurge's entire July 2002 news archive (about 11,400 words of news items, listed newest first with day headings). The Robin Hood item is headed "Strategy First to publish Robin Hood", posted by Falcon (falcon@gamesurge.com) at 4:44 am PST, under the day heading "Wednesday, July 24, 2002" (the next-older heading, "Saturday, July 20, 2002", follows immediately after it). The item reproduces a publisher press release; no score or comment counts. Retrieved directly from gamesurge.com. Commercial news content, not transcribed.

Press-release content, in order:

- Framing: Robin Hood is "a new game of tactics and action" set in a "realistic medieval environment", from "the depths of Sherwood Forest to the ramparts of Nottingham Castle".
- Backstory ("The legend of Sherwood"): England, late 12th century. King Richard the Lionhearted, back from the Crusades, is held prisoner at "Durensteien Castle" in Austria (spelling as in the release); his ransom is exorbitant. Prince John has taken the throne with the help of powerful Norman barons; extortion, racketeering, taxation and unjust laws follow. North of Nottingham, in Sherwood Forest, a rebel and outstanding archer calling himself Robin Hood refuses to give in.
- Player goal: sworn to return the throne to King Richard, the player must collect enough gold to pay the ransom and chase Prince John from the kingdom.
- Mission count and types: "over 40 separate missions of three different types":
  - Robbery and Infiltration: enter enemy castles to seize riches amassed by the Normans; free hostages; attend secret meetings; or prevent the marriage of Marian to "Guy of Guisbourne" (spelling as in the release).
  - Castle Attack: help the Saxons conquer an enemy-occupied castle by weakening strategic Norman posts so the Saxon army can invade.
  - Ambush: a smaller mission in Sherwood, stopping the tax collector's convoy by trapping and attacking its escort, or weakening enemy troops on their way to sieges.
- Team selection: before every mission the player selects five team members by their abilities; companions must not be captured or killed.
- Interface: described as simple and highly intuitive, coordinating all five characters. Example given: Friar Tuck takes down a guard while Stutely finishes setting a trap and Robin crawls between two bushes awaiting the tax collector's carriage.
- View cone: at any point the player may turn on the "view cone" or "detection cone", displayed for only one enemy at a time, to see that enemy's field of vision.
- Mood icons: small icons above the heads of all enemies in a scene show their mood: exclamation point for alarm, question mark for worry, storm cloud for annoyance, "etc." The colour shows intensity; a red exclamation point is maximum alarm.
- Mission order: no imposed linear order; several missions of different kinds are offered at once and the player may favour certain types.
- Characters: Maid Marian, Little John, Friar Tuck "and others"; new companions with special talents are recruited as the story progresses. Example: once Maid Marian is saved she joins the rebels.
- Locations: "more than nine places" modelled: Sherwood Forest, Nottingham Castle, Lincoln, York, Leicester, Derby and 3 forest intersections. Each offers one or several atmospheres: day, night or fog.
- Environment interaction: open doors, enter buildings, go upstairs, leap onto ramparts, cling to vines, set off traps, lower drawbridges, "and so on".
- Research claim: "from castle dungeons to York Cathedral" all decors were extensively researched for an authentic medieval atmosphere.
- Release window: "scheduled to hit retail stores in Winter 2002".
- Further information: www.wanadoo-edition.com and www.strategyfirst.com.

Context from the same archive page: the neighbouring items posted by Falcon the same morning are a Z-Opolis press release (4:45 am) and a moddb.com launch note (4:46 am). The July 2002 archive also contains an unrelated Strategy First item about the Jagged Alliance franchise (Sir-Tech Canada partnership), which is not about Robin Hood.
